transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start time: 15:00 EST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sofia Gomez (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Oakridge VP Eng), Amira Hassan (Oakridge Head of ML), Carlos Vega (Oakridge IT), Maya Ortiz (PM)

[00:00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time today. This is the Redwood onboarding kickoff for Oakridge health, I'll do a quick intro and then hand over to Priya and Sofia for the technical and ops bits.

[00:00:30] Jordan Lee: Thanks Liam, and thanks team. We are excited to get started, short context — Oakridge is rolling out a patient-sentiment assistant and clinical note summarization, so latency and PHI handling are top of mind.

[00:01:05] Sofia Gomez: Great, Jordan. Quick run through of agenda: 1) align on success criteria and timeline; 2) access and networking; 3) pilot scope and metrics; 4) security and compliance; 5) next steps. Sound good?

[00:01:30] Amira Hassan: Yep that works. For us the main success criteria are: P95 latency under 300ms for mid-size prompts, cost per 1k tokens under our target, and zero retention of PHI in hosted logs — or we want private deployment if not possible.

[00:02:05] Priya Nair: Thanks Amira. Quick note on options — we support Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For PHI-heavy workloads most enterprise customers go with Private or Dedicated with strict logging turned off. We can map those options to your latency and cost targets.

[00:02:40] Carlos Vega: On the security side we need SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, SAML SSO integration, and KMS integration. Also need to know if we can keep KV cache and any logs inside our VPC — we usually cannot have tokenized patient identifiers leave the VPC.

[00:03:10] Priya Nair: Understood. We have a SOC 2 report we can share. For KMS we support customer-managed keys, and for Private mode the control plane can be customer-managed with all audit logs streaming to your SIEM. Quick caveat: hosted mode retains some telemetry for billing unless you opt for dedicated/private contracts.

[00:03:45] Jordan Lee: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? Performance wise. We need consistent P95s, can't have noisy neighbors.

[00:04:05] Priya Nair: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for you — predictable throughput, isolated from multi-tenant variance. Private is fully in your VPC or on-prem with a customer-managed control plane; that gives you the most control but requires more setup. Dedicated has SLAs and is faster to stand up.

[00:04:30] Maya Ortiz: Timeline question — what does a typical pilot timeline look like? We have Q4 goals and want to be live with a narrow pilot in ~6 weeks.

[00:04:55] Sofia Gomez: Six weeks is feasible if we go Dedicated as it's faster. Private adds 2-4 weeks for networking and KMS setup, depending on your infra team availability. For a first pilot we recommend Dedicated in staging, then migrate to Private if policy requires.

[00:05:30] Amira Hassan: Ok. For the pilot we want to test our summarization model with ~3k prompts and synthetic PHI, measure latency, hallucination rates, and token cost. We'll also want to run end-to-end with our app in a staging environment.

[00:06:10] Priya Nair: That works. We'll provide a benchmark harness you can run in staging that reports P50/P95, tokens per request, and cost estimates using our unit pricing. We'll also run an initial run from our side to validate baseline numbers.

[00:06:42] Carlos Vega: On networking, we typically require VPC peering and an allowlist of Redwood egress IPs, or a private endpoint. Which one do you support?

[00:07:00] Priya Nair: We support both: VPC peering for Dedicated/Private and private endpoints for Hosted with Private Link-type setups. For Dedicated we can provide static egress ranges — I'll follow up with exact IP ranges.

[00:07:30] Jordan Lee: What about data retention — you mentioned telemetry for billing. Can we opt out and have all logs disabled?

[00:07:45] Liam Chen: Short answer: yes for Dedicated/Private we can disable application-level logs and provide only billing aggregates. For hosted free tiers we retain more telemetry. We'll send the retention policy and SOC docs as part of the security packet.

[00:08:20] Maya Ortiz: Sounds good. Also curious about model versioning — how do rollouts work? We can't have production regressions.

[00:08:40] Priya Nair: We have model pinning and rollout controls. You can pin a model version per route and do canary rollouts with traffic split and automatic fallback. Redwood Optimize will also recommend quantization and batching profiles for cost/latency tradeoffs.

[00:09:10] Amira Hassan: Is the Optimize tool an additional cost? We want to budget for licensing.

[00:09:25] Liam Chen: It's an add-on; I'll include the pricing tiers in the deck. For pilots we usually include a limited Optimize trial so you can see immediate cost wins.

[00:09:55] Priya Nair: Quick technical question for Amira — what's your average prompt length and expected session lengths so we can size KV cache needs?

[00:10:10] Amira Hassan: Average prompt is ~400 tokens, summaries up to 2k tokens once you include context. Sessions could have warm caches if a patient has multiple interactions.

[00:10:35] Priya Nair: Got it. For that profile we recommend enabling prefix caching and a medium-size KV cache on Dedicated; that should help hit your P95 targets. We'll also test quantized model variants if cost is a concern.

[00:11:10] Carlos Vega: Regarding KMS and HSM, do you support customer-managed HSM? We have FIPS requirements for certain keys.

[00:11:25] Priya Nair: We integrate with cloud KMS providers and can support customer-managed keys; HSM-level integrations depend on deployment mode, Private gives the most options. We'll capture exact compliance requirements and map them in a runbook.

[00:12:00] Jordan Lee: On governance — do you offer role based access control and audit trails for model changes and who called what?

[00:12:15] Sofia Gomez: Yes we have RBAC and detailed audit logs in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we provide audit trails but long-term retention and export to your SIEM is an enterprise add-on.

[00:12:45] Maya Ortiz: Can we get a demo of the Console to see per-route latency breakdowns and token-level cost?

[00:13:00] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll schedule a demo. Priya: action to run a short Console walkthrough and show dashboards.

[00:13:20] Liam Chen: Let's talk pilot scope and responsibilities. Suggested pilot: 2-week Dedicated staging run, 3k prompts from Amira's test set, Redwood runs baseline and shares report, Oakridge runs app-integration test. Agreement on metrics: P95 < 300ms, token cost < $5 per 1k (example).

[00:14:00] Amira Hassan: That sounds right — we'll confirm the exact cost target after seeing baseline. Also want to include hallucination checks via our eval harness.

[00:14:30] Priya Nair: Good — we'll support the eval harness; SE will help instrument.

[00:14:50] Carlos Vega: On the legal side, we have a standard DPA and need to run that by procurement. How long does contracting usually take?

[00:15:05] Liam Chen: For Dedicated pilots we typically have a short Statement of Work and MSA addendum; procurement varies but for most customers it takes 2-4 weeks. We'll coordinate with your procurement lead.

[00:15:30] Jordan Lee: Are there any known gotchas in onboarding we should plan for?

[00:15:45] Priya Nair: Common blockers: network/firewall changes, SSO metadata exchange delays, and providing representative prompts/data for the pilot. Also sometimes teams underestimate the time for KMS and audit-log export setup. We try to capture these in the onboarding checklist.

[00:16:20] Sofia Gomez: I'll send that onboarding checklist right after the call and we'll propose a week-by-week plan.

[00:16:35] Maya Ortiz: Great. One more question — can you run a quick sample benchmark now or do we need separate creds?

[00:16:50] Priya Nair: We can demo synthetic numbers, but for accurate numbers we need staging access. We'll provision a staging API key for your team and a Redwood-run job. I'll follow up with the exact steps.

[00:17:20] Liam Chen: Ok, let's recap the main commitments and owners. Sofia will share checklist and success template; Liam will send pricing and pilot SOW; Priya will provision staging and schedule a technical deep dive; Carlos will provide network details and SSO admins; Amira and Maya will finalize prompt set and evaluation metrics.

[00:17:50] Jordan Lee: That works. Any blockers for those owners?

[00:18:00] Carlos Vega: We may need a short nondisclosure addendum before sharing certain network diagrams with Redwood — procurement asks that.

[00:18:10] Liam Chen: Noted. We'll have our legal mirror and sign a mutual NDA if needed; I'll loop in legal.

[00:18:30] Amira Hassan: Timeline check: If we finalize items by Nov 10, can we start staging benchmarks the week of Nov 15?

[00:18:45] Priya Nair: Yes that's realistic for Dedicated — assuming network access is cleared. Private would push to later.

[00:19:10] Maya Ortiz: Anything else on compliance? We want to see the SOC 2 and encryption docs.

[00:19:25] Sofia Gomez: We'll put together a security packet (SOC 2, penetration test summary, KMS integration notes). Expect that in the next 2 business days.

[00:19:45] Jordan Lee: Quick FYI: we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI earlier; Anthropic had better safety controls but higher cost. We're open to Redwood if the cost/latency tradeoffs look good.

[00:20:05] Liam Chen: Totally — we'll benchmark against open baselines and show the numbers.

[00:20:30] (brief side conversation, audio overlap)

[00:21:10] Priya Nair: Technical deep-dive topics we'll cover in follow-up: model variants and quantization, batching strategies, KV cache sizing, kernel optimizations on GPU, and the deployment playbook for Dedicated.

[00:21:40] Amira Hassan: For quantization, we need to know expected quality delta vs int8. We'll want to run both to see tradeoffs.

[00:21:55] Priya Nair: Absolutely — we'll include quality regressions in the eval and tie alerts to the prompt set.

[00:22:20] Carlos Vega: For logs, we need to know how long Redwood keeps traces and whether we can push them to our S3 for e-discovery.

[00:22:35] Sofia Gomez: We can export audit logs to your S3 or SIEM in Dedicated/Private. Default retention policies are in the packet.

[00:23:00] Jordan Lee: Ok, anything else?

[00:23:10] (silence, people checking notes)

[00:23:30] Liam Chen: I think that's a wrap. Sofia will send the checklist + security packet; Priya will follow up with staging access and tech deep dive times; I'll send pricing and SOW draft. Carlos and Amira will share the required infra and prompt set.

[00:23:55] Maya Ortiz: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.

[00:24:05] Jordan Lee: Thanks team. Talk soon.

Summary (auto):
- Pilot recommended: 2-week Dedicated staging run, measure P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
- Security: SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS supported; Private mode available for full control.
- Next steps: Redwood to share onboarding & security docs, provisioning of staging, customer to provide network and evaluation data.

Notes on transcription: minor speaker attribution issues may exist; product names like "Redwood Dedicated" were sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Dedi".
